front: Monday's eight-game slate broke open at the top and blew out at the bottom. Wembanyama scored 40 with 9 blocks in only 25 minutes of San Antonio's 26-point win, Davis came back from his ankle for 44, Flagg added 43, and Golden State's 51-point win held Curry to 21 minutes. Late news took Toronto and the Lakers out of the morning grades: Barnes (Questionable at your morning lock) and Reaves (untagged then) were both ruled out before the afternoon lock. Your 95 teams (38 drafted in the morning, 57 in the afternoon) had a median finish in the top 37%; 11 made the top 10%, none the top 1%, the best finished in the top 2.4%, and 26 cashed, returning $303 on $455 in entries. The lesson is in the morning: you pushed two Questionable players down against the morning rule (a Questionable player keeps his tier), Davis from 11th on the button to 17th and Murray from 18th to 24th, and both played big (61 and 51 fantasy points), which is most of why your morning board picked the right player on only 24% of the pairs where it disagreed with our projection (55% on the season). The season pattern held too: raises on players whose game turned into a blowout are now 1 right and 16 wrong. Nothing to decide today; the flat blowout trim is retired as you asked.

moves.2: Five of the six morning moves were one idea: Davis, Questionable at the morning lock, dropped behind Reaves, Lendeborg, Kessler and Booker. He played 34 minutes for 61 points, and Reaves was ruled out later.
moves.3: Three of the five morning moves pushed Murray, Questionable at the morning lock, behind Jerome, Boozer and Thompson; he played through it for 51 points.

card: The 1/2-turn fallers didn't pay last night (1 of 13 teams in the top 10%), but that's one night against a season that has proven them.
